claims.text: Chemical dealloying of a pre-alloyed NM-HEA precursor can produce a three-dimensional nanoframework catalyst.
The resulting nanoframework has enhanced surface area relative to the precursor.
The resulting nanoframework has enhanced catalytic performance relative to the precursor.
The proposed precursor is a bulk, homogeneously mixed NM-HEA containing both noble and less noble metals.
An acid or alkali etchant can selectively dissolve the less noble components of the NM-HEA.
Controlling temperature, etchant concentration, and reaction time can prevent over-etching and structural collapse.
Selective removal of less noble metals generates an interconnected porous nanoframework.
Selective removal of less noble metals enriches the residual structure in noble metals.
Selective chemical etching of auxiliary elements leaves a continuous, high-surface-area scaffold.
Atomic-level mixing of the retained noble components provides diverse catalytic active sites.
The undealloyed precursor has a dense microstructure with lower accessible surface area than the proposed nanoframework.
Overly aggressive dealloying conditions may collapse the nanoframework.
Dealloying conditions that are too mild may produce insufficient porosity.
The dynamics of dealloying in NM-HEAs are not fully understood.
Precise control over pore size and pore distribution may vary between dealloying conditions.
